## Purpose

This SOP describes the measurement of soil microbial respiration using
the Solvita CO~2~ burst test. The method quantifies CO~2~ evolution from
rewetted, air-dried soil as an index of microbial activity and labile
carbon availability [@haney2008comparison; @haney2008estimating].

The CO~2~ burst exploits the "Birch effect," the well-documented pulse
of microbial respiration that occurs when dry soil is rapidly rewetted
[@birch1958; @fierer2003]. Drying and rewetting disrupts soil
aggregates, lyses a fraction of the microbial biomass, and releases
intracellular osmolytes, all of which provide readily mineralizable
substrate that surviving microbes respire as CO~2~ [@fierer2002;
@xiang2008]. The magnitude of the burst integrates microbial biomass
size, community physiological status, and the pool of labile organic
carbon, making it a useful single-number indicator of biological soil
fertility [@haney2008estimating].

## Scope

- **Applies to:** Air-dried, sieved soil samples collected per
  [SOP-F400](../field_sops/SOP-F400-soil-sampling.qmd) for microbial
  activity assessment
- **Does not apply to:** Compost maturity testing (see
  [SOP-L413](SOP-L413-solvita-compost-maturity.qmd)); field-moist basal
  respiration; long-term (7--28 day) incubation-based respirometry; or
  chamber-based field CO~2~ flux measurements (see
  [SOP-F406](../field_sops/SOP-F406-soil-respiration-chambers.qmd))
- **Location:** EA Program laboratory, SGM 133

## Responsibilities

| Role | Responsibility |
|:----------------------|:------------------------------------------------|
| Lab PI | Approve protocol, ensure training compliance |
| Lab Manager | Maintain Solvita kit inventory, verify probe expiration dates |
| Trained Personnel | Perform assay, record and report results |
| New Students | Complete training before independent use |

## Safety and Hazards

::: callout-warning
### Hazards

- **Physical:** Minor risk of glass breakage from incubation jars.
  Handle jars carefully; clean up broken glass with a brush and dustpan,
  not bare hands.
- **Biological:** Soil samples may contain soil-borne pathogens. Wash
  hands thoroughly after handling soil. Do not touch your face during
  the procedure.
:::

### Required PPE

- [ ] Nitrile gloves
- [ ] Safety glasses
- [ ] Lab coat

## Equipment and Materials

| Item | Notes |
|:----------------------------|:------------------------------------------|
| Solvita CO~2~ burst test kit | Should include enough probes for all samples, duplicates and controls. |
| Solvita Digital Color Reader (DCR) | For quantifying gel color change; calibrate before each batch |
| Incubation jars (475 mL) | Glass jars with screw-top lids |
| 30 cc soil scoop | Provided with kit |
| Small beakers | Can be plastic or glass. Must fit inside incubation jar |
| Analytical balance | Capable of 0.1 g resolution |
| Graduated cylinder (50 mL) or pipette | For adding deionized water |
| Deionized water | From Milli-Q system or equivalent |
| Incubator or controlled room | Set to 25 +/- 1 C |
| Timer | 24-hour countdown |
| Lab notebook or data sheet | For recording results |

## Procedure

### Sample Preparation

1.  Use soil that has been collected per
    [SOP-F400](../field_sops/SOP-F400-soil-sampling.qmd).
2.  If samples were stored at 4 C after sieving, allow them to
    equilibrate to room temperature (20--25 C) for at least 30 minutes
    before beginning the assay.
3.  Sieve soils through a 2mm sieve. Use a mortar and pestle to break up
    soil clumps that did not pass through the sieve initially and
    resieve it. Discard any rocks or other materials that do not pass
    through the sieve.

::: callout-note
The CO~2~ burst test is designed for air-dried soil. Drying standardizes
the starting moisture across samples and maximizes the rewetting
response. Results from field-moist soil are not comparable to published
Solvita norms [@solvita2019].
:::

### Incubation Setup

1.  Measure 30ccs of the dried and sieved soils using a 30cc volume
    scoop and add it to a small beaker. Weight the soil (do not include
    weight of beaker) and record the exact mass to 0.1 g. Shake it
    gently to level the surface.
2.  Gently sprinkle 9ccs of deionized water onto the surface of the soil
    using a pipette. The rewetting triggers the microbial CO~2~ burst
    [@fierer2003].
3.  Remove a fresh CO~2~-sensitive gel probe from its sealed foil
    packet. Inspect the gel: it should be attached to the probe, uniform
    in color with no cracks, discoloration, or signs of prior exposure.
    Discard compromised probes. Make sure not to touch the gel while
    handling the probe.
4.  Insert the probe into the jar so that the gel face is exposed to the
    headspace above the soil surface. Do not bury the probe in soil.
5.  Seal the jar immediately and securely.
6.  Record the jar number, sample ID, soil mass, water volume added, and
    start time.

### Incubation

1.  Place sealed jars in the incubator set to 25 +/- 1 C
2.  Incubate undisturbed for 24 hours
3.  Do not open or move jars during incubation

### Reading Results

1.  After exactly 24 hours (+/- 15 minutes), remove the gel probe from
    the jar
2.  Immediately insert the probe into the Solvita Digital Color Reader
    (DCR) and record the numerical reading
3.  Record the color number and the corresponding CO~2~-C concentration
    (mg CO~2~-C kg^-1^ soil) from the DCR or the Solvita conversion
    table

::: callout-tip
### Tip

Read probes promptly after removing them from the jar. Prolonged
exposure to ambient air will alter the gel color and compromise the
reading. The manufacturer recommends reading within 2 minutes of opening
the jar.
:::

### Calculating Results

Express results on a dry-soil basis:

$$\text{CO}_2\text{-C (mg kg}^{-1}\text{)} = \frac{\text{DCR reading (mg CO}_2\text{-C)}}{\text{oven-dry soil mass (kg)}}$$

If the oven-dry mass is not known, calculate it from the air-dried mass
and the gravimetric moisture content of a companion subsample determined
by [SOP-L400](SOP-L400-soil-moisture.qmd).

### Cleanup

1.  Dispose of used soil in the designated waste container (return to
    field site if uncontaminated, or standard trash)
2.  Wash incubation jars thoroughly with soap and water; rinse with
    deionized water; dry completely before reuse
3.  Dispose of used gel probes in standard trash

## Quality Control

### Routine QC

| QC Element | Requirement |
|:--------------------------------|:--------------------------------------|
| Duplicates | At least 1 per 10 samples; duplicates should agree within 15% relative percent difference (RPD) |
| Control | One empty, sealed jar with gel probe per batch; probe should read at or near baseline |
| Incubator temperature | Verify and record at start and end of each 24 h period; must be 25 +/- 1 C |
| DCR calibration | Calibrate per manufacturer instructions before each batch |
| Gel probe storage | Store sealed in foil packets at room temperature, away from light; check expiration dates before use |

### Corrective Actions

- If the blank reading exceeds the baseline by more than one color
  increment, check for CO~2~ contamination sources (e.g., proximity to
  gas burners, poor jar seals) and repeat the batch
- If duplicate RPD exceeds 15%, re-run the sample pair. Persistent poor
  precision may indicate sample heterogeneity; increase the number of
  subsamples

## Data Interpretation

The CO~2~ burst is proportional to microbial biomass and labile carbon
and is correlated with potential carbon, nitrogen, and phosphorus
mineralization [@haney2008estimating]. Typical ranges for the Solvita
CO~2~ burst test on agricultural and wildland soils are given below,
adapted from @haney2008comparison and the Solvita technical literature
[@solvita2019]:

| CO~2~-C (mg kg^-1^) | Interpretation | Implication |
|:-------------------|:------------------|:--------------------------------|
| \< 20 | Very low | Severely depleted microbial activity; very low labile C |
| 20--50 | Low | Limited biological activity; management intervention may be needed |
| 50--100 | Moderate | Adequate microbial activity for many soils |
| 100--150 | High | Active microbial community; good labile C supply |
| \> 150 | Very high | Highly active soil; common in recently amended or high-organic soils |

::: callout-important
These thresholds are general guidelines. Interpret results in the
context of soil type, land use, climate, and management history.
Comparisons are most meaningful when made across treatments within a
single study using the same sampling and analytical protocol.
:::

## Waste Disposal

| Waste Type            | Disposal Method                        |
|:----------------------|:---------------------------------------|
| Used soil             | Return to field site or standard trash |
| Used gel probes       | Standard trash                         |
| Deionized water rinse | Drain                                  |
| Incubation jars       | Wash, rinse, and reuse                 |

## Training Record

Before performing this assay independently, personnel must:

1.  Read this SOP in full
2.  Complete [SOP-L002 Laboratory
    Safety](SOP-L002-laboratory-safety.qmd) training
3.  Complete [SOP-F400 Soil
    Sampling](../field_sops/SOP-F400-soil-sampling.qmd) training (for
    sample preparation context)
4.  Review the Solvita CO~2~ Burst protocol sheet included in the kit
5.  Observe a trained operator perform the full procedure (setup through
    DCR reading)
6.  Perform the assay under supervision with acceptable QC results
    (duplicate RPD within 15%; blank within acceptable range)
7.  Be signed off by the PI or lab manager
